absent: Numeric value, derivation and update rules for the user address limit and page size referenced by range checks.
Exact semantics, nesting rules and fault interaction of supervisor access toggling and speculation-safe user windows.
Feature detection and fallback behavior for bulk-move and bulk-store selection, including fast string and linear-address-masking capabilities.
Per-CPU untag mask initialization, update and width, and target descriptor mask lifecycle for remote normalization.
Full layouts of the register save area, stack descriptors, task and address-space structures referenced by unwind and untag logic.
Unwind iteration beyond start, including stepping, error propagation and backend selection among table, frame-pointer and guessing variants.
Cache-line size discovery and cache-cleaning primitive guarantees for flush-aware copies.
Confidential-memory acceptance protocols, address alignment requirements and non-fatal error handling beyond the fatal dispatch shown.
Write-check and fault-annotation contracts for destination validation and potential-fault marking.
Alternate access-validation configuration body and its selection conditions.

findings.text: unsafe_copy_to_user provides a width-descending user copy primitive built from a looping helper. The loop emits one fault-checked store per element of the current width while the remainder covers that width, advancing both cursors and shrinking the remainder. The outer helper captures its arguments into locals then applies the loop at four widths from widest to narrowest, leaving any fault handling to a caller-supplied label.

arch_get_kernel_nofault and arch_put_kernel_nofault offer fault-tolerant kernel load and store helpers that reuse the sized user-access machinery with an address-space override. One load form threads the caller error label directly into the primitive; a second load form captures a local status and branches to the label only on failure; the store form threads the label directly. All are parameterized by destination, source and type so width follows the type.

The 32-bit raw_copy_to_user and raw_copy_from_user entry points forward in both directions to a common low-level routine with an address-space cast. The observable contract is residual-based: the result reports how many bytes were not transferred, with zero meaning full success.

__copy_user_ll executes inside a speculation-safe user-access window that is always closed before returning. It selects between a compact move sequence and an Intel-optimized sequence using an alignment and length predicate, then returns the residual count from whichever path ran.

The 32-bit __copy_user and __copy_user_intel sequences provide per-instruction fault recovery that converts a faulting position into a residual length. The compact form handles a short unaligned head with byte moves, a bulk middle with word moves, and a short tail with byte moves. The optimized form processes large inputs in wide fixed blocks with early size checks, then finishes with word and byte tails. Faults anywhere land on a common exit that reports what remains.

__untagged_addr normalizes user pointers that may carry tag bits. The local form applies a processor-gated mask drawn from per-CPU untag state, leaving non-supporting processors unchanged. The remote form derives the mask from the target address space descriptor. Thin wrappers preserve the caller type while delegating to these normalizers.

__access_ok validates a user range against a constant user limit. Small compile-time-known sizes need only check the base. Larger or dynamic sizes add the length to the base and require both that the sum stays within the limit and that the addition did not wrap. The base limit comparison is expressed as a likely in-range pointer check.

mask_user_address clamps an arbitrary user pointer into range with a branchless selection between the incoming value and the user limit, so out-of-range inputs saturate at the limit. A combined helper applies this clamp, opens a user-access window, and yields the sanitized pointer for immediate use.

copy_user_generic implements the 64-bit generic user copy under explicit supervisor protection toggling. The bulk transfer uses a feature-gated choice between a fast repeated move and a fallback routine, with a single fault entry that preserves the residual count. Raw directional entry points are thin wrappers that forward with an address-space cast and return the same residual.

copy_from_user_inatomic_nontemporal provides an atomic-context nontemporal copy from user whose contract combines destination validation, source sanitization and supervisor-gated bulk transfer. The observable effect is a nontemporal move with residual return, with source clamping ensuring only in-range addresses are touched and destination checking performed before any access.

copy_to_nontemporal moves through alignment, bulk, and narrowing tail phases with fault exits at each stage. Misaligned starts are normalized with small cached accesses until quadword alignment. Aligned bulk proceeds in wide unrolled iterations using paired loads and non-temporal stores. Early-load faults retry in narrower form with headway adjustment, store faults complete immediately with position-adjusted residuals, and the tail descends through quadword, long, word and byte steps with ordering enforcement before cached tails. All exits report remaining length.

copy_user_flushcache offers a cache-aware user copy that pairs a masked access window with the nontemporal engine and returns its residual. After the move it conditionally cleans cache lines only where the transfer could have used cached stores: small transfers clean unless exactly an aligned four-byte unit, while larger transfers clean a line when the start is misaligned or when the unaligned tail length is not a multiple of the wide unit.

__clear_user and clear_user clear user memory with checked and unchecked forms sharing a residual contract where the result counts bytes left uncleared. The checked form guarantees no touch on range validation failure, reporting the full length. The unchecked form assumes prior validation and performs a supervisor-gated zeroing move with feature-selected bulk store and table-driven fault exit.
fixup_umip_exception exposes a user-mode instruction prevention fixup hook that in this configuration performs no recovery and always reports that no fixup occurred.

arch_accept_memory accepts physical memory ranges on confidential-computing hosts by dispatching on platform capability: one confidential guest type uses its acceptance call with a fatal error on failure, another uses its own acceptance call, and any other platform fails fatally as unknown. A companion lookup returns no table when the firmware reports an invalid sentinel, otherwise a direct-mapped pointer to the reported table.

NR_syscalls declares the x86 syscall selection interface: total, 32-bit compat and extended counts aliasing the generated tables, plus a wide set of legacy and compat request flags covering old stat and directory handling, alarm, advisory hints, host naming, process group, scheduling priority, old mount and limit and naming queries, pause, signal set handling, multiplexed socket and IPC entry, 32-bit time variants, wait, and process creation variants including fork, virtual fork and clone, alongside compat vectored read and write variants.

Defines standard one-shot include guards for the 32-bit and 64-bit user-access headers, the mode-instruction-prevention header, the unaccepted-memory header, the syscall-number header and the unwind header, plus runtime_const_ptr as an identity helper for runtime-constant user-limit references that simply yields its argument.

unwind_state lays out unwinder state with a common prefix of stack description, stack mask, target task, graph index, error flag and optional rethook cursor, followed by a configuration-selected tail: full register tracking with stack, base and instruction pointers for table-driven unwinding, base-pointer chaining with interrupt and incomplete-frame support for frame-pointer unwinding, or a single stack pointer for the guessing unwinder. Interrupt frame geometry is derived from the register save area as an offset to the instruction field and the size from there to the end.

unwind_done reports finished when the recorded stack type is unknown and unwind_error reports failure when the error flag is set. unwind_start resolves a missing initial frame from the task register state before delegating to the selected backend. One entry-register form returns nothing once finished, otherwise the current registers with a partial indicator that reflects full-register tracking only on table-driven builds, while an alternate build always reports no entry registers. Both global and per-module initialization are no-ops in this configuration.

unwind_recover_rethook and unwind_recover_ret_addr recover true return addresses through layered adjustment: a rethook stage maps trampoline addresses via a per-task lookup keyed by stack slot and cursor, and a graph stage first adjusts for traced calls using the task and graph index before chaining into the rethook stage.

Requires the address-space read lock to be held when normalizing a remote pointer, asserts the user-access window is open only around the actual user touch with matching begin and end or supervisor toggles, and treats cross-CPU stack reads as racy: same-task reads use checked once semantics while foreign-task reads use unchecked semantics, with a helper reporting when the target runs on another processor.

User copies and clears report residuals rather than bytes moved, so callers must treat any nonzero result as partial. Faults during bulk moves are normal and land on table-driven exits; missing a close or end after an open leaves supervisor access enabled. Untagged normalization must precede range checks on tag-capable hardware, and pointer arithmetic must be checked for wrap. Nontemporal bulk requires ordering enforcement before cached tails and explicit cache cleaning for misaligned edges. Unknown memory-acceptance platforms halt, as does a failed confidential acceptance.
